clue.text: I slip back outside for a look

indicators.note: outside means the word for slip goes around the letter I
back tells us to read the assembled letters in the opposite direction

parts.note: a slip or minor error is a lapse

explanation.surface: Someone owns up to sliding backwards while out for a look around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts LAPSE around I, giving LAIPSE; 'back' then turns the whole thing round.
explanation.definitionFit: An espial is an act of spying or catching sight, an old word for a look.

indicators.note: in a down clue covering up means the first word sits above the second

parts.note: an end is a downfall or ruin
anger is strong passion or rage

explanation.surface: A collapse is threatened while strong feeling is concealed.
explanation.definitionFit: To endanger something is to put it at risk, the verb risk as a synonym.

indicators.note: something gone astray has wandered off course, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A bank deposit someone took for granted has gone missing.
explanation.definitionFit: To posit is to put forward as an assumption, so posited means assumed.

indicators.note: a tentative attempt is not settled, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A cautious move is made about a year's reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tentative' rearranges APPROACH with Y (year); 'concerning' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apocrypha are the books excluded from some versions of the Bible.

parts.note: Joy is a girl's name, here with its possessive S
to buy on tick is to buy on credit, an informal British usage

explanation.surface: A girl's reputation or standing gives her control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On tick' is British slang for buying on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: A joystick is the lever used to control an aircraft or a computer game.

clue.text: Memorial might be erected here — not if I have any say

definitions.meaning: a gravestone or monument stands literally above someone's buried corpse

definitions.text: not if I have any say
definitions.meaning: an emphatic refusal, meaning I will never allow it

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom of fierce refusal also literally describes the site of a grave monument above one's body.

clue.text: Oracle starts to speak incomprehensible — but you listen

indicators.note: starts to means take the opening letter of each word that follows

explanation.surface: A prophet begins speaking in riddles, but listeners pay attention anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: A sibyl was a prophetess of the ancient world, an oracle who foretold events.

definitions.meaning: a nun belongs to a religious order, so she may be described as a member of one
functioning properly, as a machine in good condition

explanation.definitionFit: A nun is a member of a religious order, and the phrase also means in working condition.

parts.note: kit is a set of equipment

explanation.surface: Cheap gear is handed to a school.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitsch describes cheap, showy, tasteless art, so tawdry as an adjective.

clue.text: Approach task boldly — you may get stung

definitions.meaning: to tackle a difficult job firmly and without hesitation
literally, seizing a stinging plant carries the risk of being stung

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to tackle a difficulty boldly, literally gripping a stinging weed.

indicators.note: In tells us the cleaning word sits inside the word for end

parts.note: to die is to come to an end
to scour is to clean up by scrubbing

explanation.surface: Someone finally tidies up a chat.
explanation.definitionFit: Discourse is formal talk or discussion, a synonym for conversation.

clue.text: Raise temperature after indications of disapproval

indicators.note: after places the temperature letter following the jeers

parts.note: boos are noises showing disapproval

explanation.surface: Tempers flare after a crowd jeers.
explanation.definitionFit: To boost something is to lift or increase it, a synonym of raise.

indicators.note: wandering aimlessly about suggests the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: People of different temperaments stroll around without purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's nature is their character, so natures are characters in the plural.

indicators.note: received by means the word for look is taken inside the doctor

parts.note: a medic is a doctor
lo is an old exclamation meaning look

explanation.surface: A doctor gets a charming glance.
explanation.definitionFit: Melodic music is tuneful, and sweet describes a pleasing tune.

definitions.meaning: to finish up somewhere at last
upended, standing on one end, as when something is turned upside down

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to arrive at last, and literally describes something stood on its end.

clue.text: Line on shore — it goes round nameless country

indicators.note: goes round tells us to turn the word it backwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: nameless removes N, the abbreviation for name

parts.note: Denmark is a European country

explanation.surface: A coastal line runs around an unnamed nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes round' looks like a container signal, but here it only turns the two letters back; 'nameless' drops N, the usual abbreviation for name.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidemark is the line left on a shore by the high tide.

clue.text: Doctor has to resort to carriage in play

parts.note: MO is Medical Officer, a doctor
to resort to something is to use it
a trap is a light horse-drawn carriage

explanation.surface: A doctor is forced to take a coach during a theatre show.
explanation.walkthrough: THE MOUSETRAP is Agatha Christie's long-running London play.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mousetrap is the famous Agatha Christie murder-mystery play.

clue.text: Money — just enough for fine wool

parts.note: cash is money
mere means only or barely, just enough and no more

explanation.surface: Someone has only just enough money to buy luxury yarn.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashmere is the soft, fine wool from Kashmir goats.

clue.text: Here film is kept under wraps

definitions.text: Here film is kept under wraps

parts.words: Here film is kept under wraps
parts.note: film is literally kept in a photographic device, and a hearing held privately is kept secret, behind closed doors

explanation.definitionFit: The Latin legal phrase means in private, behind closed doors, and literally inside the device that holds film.

clue.text: Fruit 'with skin might be described as bananas

parts.note: a nut is a kind of fruit
a case is an outer covering or skin

explanation.surface: A fruit in its peel could be called a banana.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' is slang for crazy; the definition describes a person who could be called that.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutcase is a crazy person, someone you might call bananas, meaning mad.

indicators.note: selection from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A grown-up product line offers something at the far end.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultra as an adjective or noun denotes the extreme end of a range or view.

clue.text: Prepared to plead for little swimmer

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, so the letters are reworked into a new form

explanation.surface: Someone is ready to beg on behalf of a young swimmer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tadpole is a small swimming larva of a frog or toad.

definitions.meaning: an ordinary seaman in the Royal Navy, not an officer

explanation.definitionFit: A rating is both a sharp scolding and a non-commissioned sailor in the British navy.

clue.text: How to make us use embassy employee

parts.note: fixing an E onto the end of the word us turns it into the word use, so the instruction that does it is the wordplay

explanation.surface: Instructions on how to get us to use the embassy's staff.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: 'How to make' asks for the instruction that turns US into USE, which is 'attach E'; run together, that gives the diplomat.
explanation.definitionFit: An attaché is a diplomat attached to an embassy staff with a specialist role.

clue.text: Hit on the head, needing repair for damaged tooth

definitions.meaning: to strike someone on the top of the skull
a dental cap fitted over a broken tooth

explanation.definitionFit: To crown is to hit on the head, and a crown is a cap fitted on a damaged tooth.

indicators.note: before puts the money word ahead of the day's abbreviation

parts.note: bread is slang for money or cash

explanation.surface: Someone is generous with money ahead of Thursday.
explanation.definitionFit: Breadth of mind is broad tolerance, so liberality of outlook.

clue.text: State where I had a little house

parts.note: I'd is the short form of I had
HO is an abbreviation of house, as in addresses

explanation.surface: Someone recalls the US state where they once owned a small home.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is one of the states of the USA.

indicators.note: branching out suggests going off in new directions, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone expanding a business places orders for a cross-bred bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Branching' rearranges OUT and ORDERS together; 'out' looks like part of the phrase 'branching out' but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The heraldic emblem combines the red rose of Lancaster and the white rose of York, a hybrid flower.

definitions.meaning: neat is an old word for cattle, and a Channel Island breed of dairy cow is named after its island
a woolly is a knitted sweater, and a thick fisherman's jumper bears the same island name

explanation.definitionFit: The Channel Island gives its name to both a breed of cow (neat means cattle) and a heavy knitted sweater (a woolly).

parts.note: a piece is a bit or portion

explanation.surface: Everyone gets a share of something.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means for each one, as in costing a pound per item.
